clauses.name: checkOccurrenceDefinitionMultiplicitySpecialization
clauses.rule: Individual occurrences require a multiplicity specializing Base::zeroOrOne; this remains a separate dependency.

clauses.name: checkConnectionDefinitionSpecializations/checkConnectionDefinitionBinarySpecialization
clauses.rule: Connection defaults require Connections::Connection and binary definitions specialize Connections::BinaryConnection.

clauses.name: checkInterfaceDefinitionSpecialization/checkInterfaceDefinitionBinarySpecialization
clauses.rule: Interface defaults require Interfaces::Interface and binary definitions specialize Interfaces::BinaryInterface.

clauses.name: checkFlowDefinitionSpecialization/checkFlowDefinitionBinarySpecialization
clauses.rule: Flows specialize Flows::MessageAction; a flowEnd count of two requires Flows::Message. Full flowEnd derivation and complete legality remain unqualified.

normative_clauses.rule: Select owned FeatureMemberships, project their ownedMemberFeatures in order, then filter isEnd for ownedEndFeature.

imported.frontend: JDK javac parse/analyze with resolved symbols, parameter/result types, receivers and expression/statement trees. Five method bodies include the proven empty additional-member hook.
imported.generation: Bounded source translation for blocks, return, if, ternary, integer inequality, literal default keys and selected resolved calls. Runtime-selected implicit-general names bind each metaclass. Unsupported calls, types or member algorithms fail closed.

dependencies: definition_owned_features: handwritten Ecore-driven ordered canonical ownership/end derivation with imported delegate/target/subset checks
stored_definition_generalizations: handwritten explicit-plus-default combination, self exclusion, endpoint validation and conservative metadata guard
definition_inherited_memberships: shared inherited lookup and concrete pending-field scheduling
standard_default_binding: canonical standard-library membership lookup; prior provider disagreements remain explicit

verification.scope: Actual Pilot selector/general-type observations across 26 concrete Definition metaclasses, individual false/true where available and zero through three owned ends. Library bindings are supplied only for these factory controls. Contexts exercise selector behavior, including shapes that may violate later language constraints; these controls do not qualify full models or validation.
verification.native_checks: All controls execute the generated policy, owned-end computation and typed generalization consumer; reversed record order, missing libraries, wrong target kinds and incomplete canonical inputs are checked.
verification.persistence: Every matched document is compared after JSON persistence/reload.

unsupported_required_behavior: Individual source adds an unnamed Multiplicity via the pinned grammar. Shared Feature naming now handles it; a retained Pilot model still differs at Usage.isVariable because Usage.mayTimeVary remains unimplemented. This model is not counted as matching; full individual-definition support remains open.
Feature inheritance/redefinition, Usage defaults, semantic metadata, full standard-library/global-resource loading and language validation remain required.
All 26 selector programs have bounded runtime evidence; this does not qualify every textual declaration family or each default target library implementation.

The written Flow rule tests flowEnd whereas the pinned Java selector reads ownedEndFeature. The matching source context has owned ends only. Inherited Feature/end traversal still rejects pending redefinition filtering; equivalence outside this scope is unqualified and must be resolved normatively.
No full sample, release-wide semantic or timing gate is closed.
positional_end_integration_boundary: Generic positional end naming is now implemented separately. FlowDefinition with explicit generals is rejected directly by definition_default_names until the written flowEnd-count constraint and the Pilot ownedEndFeature-count selector are reconciled. The existing independent source regression checks this named dependency, rather than relying on missing generic end semantics.
